ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all ultimate beneficial owners, directors, shareholders above the 25 percent threshold, and authorized signatories against: (i) the consolidated United Nations Security Council sanctions list; (ii) the New Zealand sanctions measures administered under the Russia Sanctions Act 2022 and the Sanctions (United Nations) Regulations 2004; (iii) the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit designated persons list; (iv) the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List as a prudent global standard; and (v) the United Kingdom and European Union consolidated financial sanctions lists. Politically exposed persons, including domestic PEPs as redefined by the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Definitions) Amendment Act 2023, trigger mandatory enhanced due diligence, senior management approval for any business relationship, and ongoing enhanced transaction monitoring. The company must maintain a risk-based AML/CFT compliance programme covering customer due diligence, ongoing monitoring, suspicious transaction reporting, and annual staff training, consistent with the medium-risk enhanced AML/CFT classification attributed to the public commercial web scraping and data-pipeline API industry.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office Online Register (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz), accessed through RealMe identity authentication
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in the English or Maori language using the Roman (Latin) alphabet without diacritical marks; the name must end with the suffix Limited, Ltd, or the Maori form Tapui (Limited); punctuation is limited to spaces, ampersand, period, comma, apostrophe, plus sign, and hyphen; numerals may be used; a transliteration into a non-Latin script is not permitted on the official register, and any foreign-language variant must be a direct transliteration submitted as a trading name rather than the registered entity name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank (requires prior consent of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand under the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989)
Insurance / Insurer / Assurance (requires prior consent of the Financial Markets Authority)
Trust / Trustee / Unit Trust (requires ministerial or regulatory consent given fiduciary implications)
Building Society (restricted under the Building Societies Act 1965)
Chartered (implies an affiliation with a professional or royal body and requires proof of such affiliation)
Royal / Crown / Government / National / New Zealand Government (implies official patronage and requires ministerial approval)
University / Polytechnic / Institute of Technology (requires authorization from the Ministry of Education)
Incorporated / Inc. (prohibited as a company suffix in New Zealand; only Limited or Tapui (Limited) is permitted for limited liability companies)
Council / Association / Chamber (likely to be refused if it implies a public authority or if the name is otherwise misleading under section 24 of the Companies Act 1993)
Co-operative (restricted under the Co-operative Companies Act 1996)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is valid for 20 working days from the date of reservation; within that period the applicant must file the incorporation application. If further time is required, the applicant may file a new reservation immediately or, where the Companies Office permits, request an administrative re-reservation without re-payment; there is no statutory extension mechanism under the Companies Act 1993. Upon a notice of name rejection, the applicant must submit a written Request for Reconsideration to the Registrar of Companies at the New Zealand Companies Office (Wellington) within 20 working days of the notice, citing the facts supporting non-conflict, including trademark coexistence consent letters, letters of no objection from any incumbent holder, and evidence that the name is not misleading or contrary to section 22(2) of the Companies Act 1993. If the Registrar confirms the rejection, the applicant may pursue judicial review of the decision before the High Court of New Zealand under the Senior Courts Act 2016, with an application to be filed within 28 days of the final administrative refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. The Companies Act 1993 section 189 requires every company to maintain a registered office in New Zealand with a physical street address where documents may be served and received during ordinary business hours. A P.O. Box address alone is prohibited. A licensed registered-office services provider or corporate services agent offering a virtual office is acceptable for this data-pipeline and web-scraping API business, provided the provider maintains a genuine physical presence in New Zealand, accepts service of process, and provides mail forwarding and statutory document handling. The virtual office will not satisfy IRD commercial substance expectations for New Zealand domestic corporate tax residence purposes if the entity derives New Zealand-sourced revenue, but it is sufficient for registration and legal compliance purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate: approximately 20 percent probability of an unannounced on-site compliance verification within the first 12 months of registration if the company is classified as a financial service provider or reporting entity under the AML/CFT Act 2009 by reason of accepting cryptocurrency (USDC) and Stripe payment rails. The New Zealand Companies Office, the Financial Markets Authority, and the Department of Internal Affairs conduct risk-based targeted inspections, with enhanced attention on entities in the medium-risk enhanced AML/CFT tier. For a pure API reseller with no New Zealand-sourced revenue and no New Zealand employees, the inspection probability reduces to approximately 5 to 10 percent, but any involvement in virtual-asset transfers or money remittance materially elevates the risk.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), sections 12 to 20 (incorporation and certificate of incorporation), sections 21 to 23 (company names), sections 24 to 35 (share capital and shareholder rights), sections 126 to 134 (registered office and constitution), and sections 145 to 153 (board and director appointments); Financial Reporting Act 2013 and Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 apply where relevant.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, an agency within the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating the New Zealand Companies Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Online application for registration of a company filed through the New Zealand Companies Office 'Register a company' electronic portal, resulting in a Certificate of Incorporation and allocation of a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; a company limited by shares may issue one or more shares for nominal or nil consideration. There is no capital escrow, deposit, or paid-up capital verification requirement at incorporation. The subscribers must disclose the number of shares issued, class, and amount paid or unpaid on the incorporation application; full payment, if any, is settled by agreement with the board.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED, registered under the Companies Act 1993 of New Zealand. RESOLVED as follows: 1. The proposed allocation and subscription of ordinary shares as set out in the incorporation application are approved, and the board hereby subscribes for, issues, and allots those shares to the named subscribers at the stated nominal consideration, fully or partly paid as recorded in the share register. 2. The registered office of the Company is fixed and adopted at [street address, city, New Zealand], and the directors are instructed to maintain the registered office and records at that address and to notify any change to the Registrar. 3. [name] is appointed as chairperson and director, [name] is appointed as chief executive officer, and [name] is appointed as company secretary, each with authority to act within the constitution and applicable law. 4. The officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute electronic payment mandates, and complete tax, IRD, client, and governmental filings on behalf of the Company. 5. The board resolves that all prior actions in preparation of the incorporation are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office – Companies Register online name search and reservation portal (RealMe-authenticated).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the New Zealand Companies Register to confirm that the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing name, does not violate a restricted word restriction, and is not prohibited under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993. If the name contains a restricted word such as 'bank', 'trust', or 'university', obtain the written consent of the relevant regulator. Reserve the selected name for up to 20 working days, then proceed with the incorporation application using the same name.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (up to three alternatives)
Statement of intended principal business purpose
Name reservation application submitted online
Regulatory consent if a restricted word is used
RealMe authenticated applicant identity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a revised name reservation with alternative names or apply to the Registrar for reconsideration of the refusal under the Companies Act 1993. If the refusal relates to a restricted word, procure the regulator’s written clearance and resubmit. A fresh incorporation application may also be filed with an approved name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of statutory incorporation documents and subscriber consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company formation agent and the New Zealand Companies Office data fields for incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the company constitution if a bespoke constitution is desired; if none is adopted, the default rules in the Companies Act 1993 apply. Determine the initial shareholder(s), share classes, and director(s). Obtain signed consent to act as director from each proposed director through the Companies Office form. Ensure that at least one director is resident in New Zealand or, alternatively, qualifies under the Australian director residency exception in section 150 of the Companies Act 1993. Confirm a physical street address in New Zealand for the registered office; a Post Office box is not acceptable. The incorporator must authenticate the application through RealMe and declare that all statutory requirements are met; notarization is not required for standard New Zealand incorporations.
required_dossiers: Signed consent to act as director for each proposed director
Constitution executed by the subscribers (if adopted)
Legal name, former name, residential and business addresses, date and place of birth of directors and shareholders
Share structure schedule showing share classes, share counts, and paid or partly paid amounts
Registered office address in New Zealand (physical street address)
Name reservation number or approved company name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the application, submit an explanatory declaration or amend the relevant data field within the response period. If an invalid director address or consent is the issue, appoint an additional New Zealand-resident director and rescind the non-resident appointment, or cure the defect before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgement of incorporation application and issue of certificate of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (companiesoffice.govt.nz) – electronic incorporation lodgement.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online incorporation application with all name, director, shareholder, registered office, share capital, and constitutional details. Attach director consent statements and any adopted constitution. Verify the accuracy of all declarations. Pay the official incorporation fee online by credit, debit, or approved electronic payment method. Upon successful processing, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation, allocates the company number, and registers the company on the New Zealand Companies Register; the company automatically receives a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). The company exists as a separate legal entity from the date shown on the certificate.
required_dossiers: Completed online incorporation application
Approved name reservation number (if reserved)
Director consent forms embedded in the application
Constitution file (if any) uploaded during lodgement
Payment of prescribed incorporation fee
RealMe authenticated digital signature of the applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects the application, correct the named defects and refile promptly. A person aggrieved by a refusal may request an internal review under the Companies Act 1993 and may ultimately appeal to the High Court. The new application fee applies unless the refusal was a manifest registrar error and the defect is immediately cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board meeting, share allotment, statutory registers, and registered office adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand board of directors; filings with the New Zealand Companies Office for any post-incorporation record changes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting and pass the First Board Resolution. Authorize the allotment of subscribed shares and issue share certificates to the initial shareholders. Confirm and adopt the registered office address as the company’s official address for service under Companies Act 1993. Appoint the chairperson, chief executive officer, company secretary, and other officers as proposed. Establish statutory registers at the registered office, including the share register, director and shareholder registers, directors’ interests register, and minute book. If the registered office differs from the address submitted at incorporation, file a notice of change with the Companies Office. Complete banking mandates and execute the opening of any settlement bank account.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution signed by the directors
Share certificates and share register
Directors' interests register and minutes of the first board meeting
Confirmation of registered office physical address
Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN confirmation
Director identification and bank account opening mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a Companies Office filing is queried, correct the register or resolution and resubmit within the notice period. If the registered office address becomes invalid, select a new physical address, pass a board resolution, and file the change of address with the Companies Office. Any missing statutory register must be reconstructed and signed by a director to restore compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, GST, PAYE, and employer registrations with Inland Revenue
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) through the myIR portal and Business.govt.nz integrated registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the company’s NZBN and Certificate of Incorporation, register the company with Inland Revenue to obtain an IRD number for income tax purposes. Register for GST if annual taxable turnover is expected to exceed NZD 60,000, or voluntarily if lower. If employees will be engaged, register for PAYE, KiwiSaver, and employer-related obligations and obtain ACC cover through ACC Business Online. Register the active business classification under NZISIC and obtain the relevant business tax numbers. The API scraping and data commerce activity does not require a separate financial services licence, but the company should document its AML/CFT risk controls if it handles crypto-asset settlement or proceeds of payment card transactions.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN confirmation
Directors' and shareholders' IRD numbers and identification details
Registered office and business address details
GST and PAYE registration application
Statement of principal business activity (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 518210)
Bank account details after account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue queries the registration, respond through myIR with additional evidence of the intended lawful data-processing activity and actual or projected turnover. If the IRD number is refused on information insufficiency, supply full director identification and business documentation, and if necessary appeal the decision to the Commissioner of Inland Revenue or seek judicial review.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board applies to this digital data-pipeline service; general market conduct is overseen by the Commerce Commission (Fair Trading Act 1986) and privacy compliance by the New Zealand Office of the Privacy Commissioner.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no statutory operating, manufacturing, or physical premises licence is required for public commercial web scraping and proxy API gateway services in New Zealand.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not applicable — the undertaking is an information technology service with no manufacturing, construction, discharge, or land-use activity listed under Schedules 1 to 4 of the Resource Management Act 1991; no EIA or resource consent is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — no industrial wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste discharge. Office waste is managed through municipal collection; electronic waste handling, if any, complies with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 and the Ozone Layer Protection Act 1996 where relevant.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No special civil defence permit or industrial clearance is required for this service activity. Any leased office premises must satisfy the fire safety and occupancy requirements under the Building Act 2004 and Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) operational guidance. The company, if it employs staff, must comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, including hazard identification, emergency procedures, and workplace training; WorkSafe New Zealand clearance is not otherwise required for an office-based information services business.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake), New Zealand Government — official national tax authority and portal: https://www.ird.govt.nz (myIR Secure portal for registrations, GST returns and taxpayer profiles). Customs-side export controls are administered by the New Zealand Customs Service (https://www.customs.govt.nz), which supports GST export documentation and border clearance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The statutory route for a foreign-incorporated International Company (CK_IC) to obtain a tax identity number is: (1) Inland Revenue issues an IRD number (non-resident company tax file number) on application using form IR596, supported by the certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, board/shareholder resolutions, director identity documents, and proof of foreign residence or tax residence; (2) once the IRD number is received, the entity activates a myIR Secure account and applies for Goods and Services Tax (GST) registration through the myIR portal (form GST101A) either mandatorily, if the 60,000 NZD threshold is exceeded, or voluntarily; (3) where the company is incorporated under the Companies Act 1993 in New Zealand, registration with the Companies Office automatically transmits particulars to Inland Revenue, which assigns an IRD number and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) without further application; (4) a CK_IC with no New Zealand fixed establishment, no New Zealand-resident management and no New Zealand-sourced income is not required to file New Zealand income tax returns, but is required to hold an IRD number and to file GST returns where New Zealand GST registration applies; (5) all registrations, returns and payments are made electronically through myIR or approved tax-agent software.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — The CK_IC International Company is classified for New Zealand tax purposes as a non-resident company operating entirely offshore; it has no New Zealand source revenue and no permanent establishment in New Zealand, therefore the 28% New Zealand corporate income tax does not apply. The New Zealand income tax system is not a territorial system for resident companies (residents are taxed on worldwide income), so the Tax_Exempt_Zone classification is conditional on non-residence under the place-of-incorporation and central-management-and-control test, together with the absence of New Zealand source income. Digital API and web-scraping subscription fees sourced from non-resident customers are not income derived from New Zealand and fall outside New Zealand income tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not maintain a check-the-box election for corporations. The applicable statutory elections and options for this entity are limited to: (1) voluntary GST registration under section 51 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 for suppliers below the 60,000 NZD threshold; (2) GST group registration under section 55 of the GST Act 1985 aggregating related companies into one GST registered group; (3) simplified non-resident supplier GST registration for remote digital services supplied into New Zealand consumers; (4) optional taxable-supply-information methods in the form of e-invoices that satisfy GST invoice requirements; (5) in income tax, New Zealand has no elective pass-through classification for International Companies — look-through company elections under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007 are reserved exclusively for closely held resident companies and are unavailable to a non-resident International Company; (6) no hybrid-mismatch or entity classification election is available for this entity.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) — the central bank and prudential supervisor of all registered banks; the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) exercises co-supervision over non-bank financial institutions and AML/CFT reporting entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates as an IMF Article 8 jurisdiction with fully liberalised current and capital accounts. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is freely convertible in the global interbank market with no exchange controls, no prior-approval mechanism, and no documentation requirements for cross-border settlement. Capital-account transactions — including the injection of equity into the CK_IC International Company, intercompany loans, and acquisition of New Zealand digital-asset infrastructure — are lawful without RBNZ approval except where the Overseas Investment Act 2005 notification threshold applies to sensitive land, fishing quota, or 25%+ control of significant business assets. Current-account items (API subscription fees, scraping-software royalties, data-gateway disbursements, and profit remittances) may be freely converted into any currency. The only substantive hurdles to profit remittance are tax-based rather than exchange-based: (i) non-resident withholding tax on dividends (15% under applicable DTA, 30% otherwise); (ii) Approved Issuer Levy for eligible interest; (iii) transfer-pricing rules under Part 8 of the Income Tax Act 2007; and (iv) thin-capitalisation interest-limitation rules that constrain debt-funded repatriation. Payments in or relating to USDC are convertible to NZD provided the conversion is executed via an FMA-supervised exchange and the receiving bank is satisfied the arrangement does not operate as an unregistered designated settlement system under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2022.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no export proceeds surrender or repatriation obligation in New Zealand. The statutory regime does not impose a timeline for bringing export receipts onshore, nor does it mandate any conversion ratio for foreign currency earned from ISIC 6201 digital-commerce activities. The CK_IC may retain USD, EUR, GBP, and USDC indefinitely in foreign-currency accounts at an RBNZ-registered bank or within segregated licensed-custody wallets, subject only to New Zealand tax valuation: the company must recognise foreign-currency balances at fair value under NZ IFRS 9 and account for any FX gains under the Income Tax Act 2007 (reporting on an accruals basis unless a functional-currency exemption has been obtained from the IRD). The reporting constraints that replace surrender rules are: (a) notifiable transaction reports to the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit for cash or digital-asset transactions above NZD 10,000; (b) bank international-transaction reporting to Statistics New Zealand for any receipt above NZD 100,000; and (c) IRD disclosure of offshore direct-investment balances above NZD 1 million. Where the exporter chooses to convert, settlement is executed through a licensed FX dealer at prevailing interbank rates without approval.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High for ancillary treasury agility, but legally constrained for primary banking. New Zealand permits foreign digital EMIs (Airwallex, Payoneer, Wise Platform, and similar providers) to serve the CK_IC through AML/CFT-registered financial service providers supervised by the Financial Markets Authority. Such EMIs provide multi-currency virtual IBANs, SWIFT receiving rails, mass-payout APIs, and instantly convertible USD/NZD/GBP/EUR pockets, making them strong candidates for Stripe-Aggregator payouts and low-value supplier disbursements. They are not registered banks and cannot take deposits, issue credit, or access the RBNZ ESAS settlement system without becoming clearing participants, so an RBNZ-registered bank must remain the settlement anchor. Specific legal constraints: (a) the EMI must hold an FMA registration number and appear on the Financial Service Providers Register; (b) an offshore EMI that is not NZ-registered can service the IC only for foreign-currency accounts, not NZD bank accounts; (c) crypto-to-fiat conversion inside an EMI may be rejected under bank de-risking policies, requiring use of a licensed NZ crypto/stablecoin exchange as an intermediate step; and (d) cross-border EMIs are subject to the Financial Market Infrastructures Act 2021 designation powers should their transaction volumes exceed systemic thresholds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No New Zealand statute obliges directors to appear physically at a bank branch. The AML/CFT Act 2009 and the Companies Act 1993 permit fully remote onboarding for medium-risk vehicles using video-verified identity, certified corporate extracts, and a notarised UBO declaration. In practice, however, the tax-exempt CK_IC combined with USDC payment rails places the entity in the 'Medium_Risk_Enhanced' category, and the major banks require at least one live video interview with a compliance officer; BNZ and ANZ will accept a fully digital interview if the sole director holds a passport from an OECD jurisdiction and the company appoints an FMA-approved New Zealand resident agent. Physical attendance at an Auckland branch remains mandatory where (i) the ultimate beneficial owner resides in a FATF dark-listed or high-risk jurisdiction, (ii) the entity seeks a Capital Escrow Account holding shareholder equity, or (iii) the bank must verify original evidence of source of wealth. The prudent blueprint is to mandate a single director journey to Auckland for the opening interview and to co-engage a licensed corporate-trust service provider pre-cleared by the bank, thereby eliminating KYC interview latency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore 'International Company' in a Tax-Exempt Zone with no demonstrated New Zealand economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance Proof Pack: Companies Office NZBN extract naming a New Zealand registered office and the Companies Act 1993 address for service; New Zealand IRD registration confirmation; lease or virtual-office agreement with a New Zealand provider; employment agreement and payroll records for a part-time New Zealand AML/CFT compliance officer; invoice from a New Zealand legal or data-security adviser; board resolution authorising the banking relationship; and six months of management accounts evidencing real business costs in New Zealand.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: USDC and cryptocurrency settlement on Stripe and blockchain rails
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Crypto Compliance Dossier: executed master-services agreement with an FMA-supervised New Zealand digital-currency exchange for USDC-to-NZD conversion; certification that the IC operates no unregistered digital-asset platform; chain-analytics reports (Chainalysis or Elliptic) demonstrating that incoming USDC addresses are free of sanctions and dark-market exposure; New Zealand legal opinion confirming that the API subscription tokens are not 'financial products' under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; customer onboarding KYC policy satisfying the AML/CFT Act 2009 travel rule; and written acknowledgement that the IC will not engage in staking, lending, or derivative use of stablecoin balances.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Medium_Risk_Enhanced industry classification for public commercial web scraping and proxy API gateways (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 518210)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Data-Commerce Compliance File: documented contractual consents, robots.txt honouring policy, and scraping-permission matrices for each targeted data source; API gateway terms of use and Privacy Act 2020-compliant privacy policy; customer agreements prohibiting unlawful or infringing use; ISO 27001 certification and a recent penetration-test report for the API infrastructure; a data-ethics legal opinion from New Zealand counsel; and traffic logs anonymised to demonstrate proportionate, non-disruptive access patterns.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership with multi-jurisdictional wire inflows and no in-country shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source of Wealth and Source of Funds bundle: audited financial statements of each direct shareholder; six months of parent-entity bank statements with reasoned transaction memos; trust deed, settlement deed, and a 25%+ beneficial-ownership attestation; sanctions and PEP screening certificates covering United Nations, OFAC, EU, UK, and New Zealand lists; notarised declaration confirming absence of politically exposed persons; and a corporate resolution segregating future inbound wires to a single dedicated Capital Escrow Account.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return to the Register of Companies (AR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Nga Kaitiaki o Take), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 31 working days after the anniversary date of incorporation (Companies Act 1993, s 210); the Companies Register generates a reminder one month before the due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: NZD 200 late-filing penalty per statutory fee schedule; if the return remains unfiled for 6 months after the due date, the Registrar must remove the company from the Register under s 318 Companies Act 1993, resulting in loss of limited liability, vesting of remaining assets in the Crown, and director disqualification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: IR4 Company Annual Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Return due 7 July following the standard 31 March balance date; tax-agent extension to 31 March of the next income year. Provisional tax instalments due 28 August, 15 January and 7 May; terminal tax due 7 February (or 7 April with an agent extension where applicable).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty NZD 250 (increasing to NZD 500 when overdue by more than one month); late-payment penalty of 1% on day 1, an additional 4% on day 8, and 1% per month thereafter; use-of-money interest (UOMI) accrues at statutory rates on unpaid tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Statutory Audit Report (Large or audited companies only)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of each financial year (Companies Act 1993, s 212), filed together with the Independent Auditor's Report where a statutory audit is triggered.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Persistent non-compliance exposes the company and its directors to Registrar enforcement, including formal default notices, court orders for compliance, and deregistration; conviction-based fines may be imposed on directors under the Companies Act 1993 for failure to comply with filing obligations.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday; R&D Tax Incentive: 15% refundable tax credit (s LV 2, LV 4, 1.5× loss-credit uplift s LV 8); possible 2% AIL for interest; (for CK_IC classification: no separate NZ 'exempt-zone' rate) ...
